nodes.name: Zerubbabel
nodes.notes:
Son of Pediah, and first kingly governor of Jerusalem post-exile. 
Because of some unrecorded circumstance, Zerubbabel is also called the son of Pedaiah’s brother Shealtiel. Shealtiel may have adopted Zerubbabel if Pedaiah died when the boy was young; or, if Shealtiel died before fathering a son, Pedaiah may have performed brother-in-law marriage, fathering Zerubbabel in the name of his brother Shealtiel.

[Inference: as Shealtiel is listed as son of Neri (son-in-law; see ‘Shealtiel’) in the genealogy in Luke 3, which is a genealogy of Jesus’ natural right to the throne, we can assume that Neri’s daughter, who is married to Shealtiel, is Zerubbabel’s birth mother. 
Since it’s listed in 1Chronicles 3:19 that Zerubbabel is Pedaiah’s son, but everywhere else Zerubbabel is named ‘son of Shealtiel’, we can infer that likely Pediah is the father of Zerubbabel by blood, having taken the wife of his brother, Shealtiel, in brother-in-law marriage after Shealtiel died without children. 
(We can assume that it was not the other way around as Pedaiah had a second son, thus brother-in-law marriage would either not have applied since he died with a child already, or if he died with no children then the account in Chronicles would not have named both children as his sons.)
The intent of brother-in-law marriage is so that the brother who died would not be forgotten in history, so the way in which Zerubbabel was named ‘son of Shealtiel’ everywhere else would follow this custom and not be in conflict.]

nodes.name: Neri
nodes.notes:
A question rises from Luke’s genealogy:
Neri is not listed as Shealtiel’s father in other genealogical accounts, where Jeconiah is Shealtiel’s father.
Since Shealtiel is listed as the direct son of Jehoiachin in the line of kings record, it is assumed that perhaps Neri is the father of Shealtiel’s wife, same as how Joseph is listed as “Son of Heli” though Heli is Mary’s father. 
This would then be consistent and still be an accurate tracing of the bloodline at Luke 3
